items.summary: Regulation inevitably involves choices.Protecting consumers and maintaining confidence in our markets are fundamental to what we do. But rules also have costs. Good regulation means recognising those trade-offs and using evidence to decide where intervention will make the biggest difference.That is why economics matters so much to good regulation.At our annual Economics Conference, economists, academics, regulators and industry experts came together to explore how smarter financial regulation can support sustainable growth and innovation.
